project.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

parsed_output.evidence: In-container run on the current (unpatched) code: `[POV] VULNERABLE: malicious entry escaped the extraction directory.` and `[POV] File written outside target: /tmp/zipslip-pov.../ESCAPED.txt` with EXIT=0. Simulated patch (canonical-path guard inserted via sed into a copy of IOUtils.java) produced `[POV] unzip threw: java.io.IOException: Zip slip: ../ESCAPED.txt` and `[POV] SAFE` with PATCHED_EXIT=1, confirming the POV distinguishes patched from unpatched.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: The POV crafts a zip containing an entry named `../ESCAPED.txt`, then calls IOUtils.unzip(zip, extractDir). On unpatched code the file is written to the PARENT of extractDir (outside the intended extraction directory), the POV prints 'VULNERABLE' and exits 0. After a correct patch that rejects entries resolving outside the extraction directory (e.g. a canonical-path prefix check), unzip throws or skips, no file escapes, the POV prints 'SAFE' and exits 1.
parsed_output.notes: The POV exercises the real project source: run_pov.sh compiles the actual one-java-agent-plugin/src/main/java/com/alibaba/oneagent/utils/IOUtils.java together with the driver and invokes IOUtils.unzip directly (IOUtils depends only on the JDK, so no Maven build is required). Files live under .security-pipeline/pov/ only; no product code or normal tests were modified. run_pov.sh recreates its own classes/ output dir on each run.
parsed_output.regression_hint: A correct fix should validate each zip entry's resolved destination against the canonical path of the extraction directory (reject/skip entries whose canonical path does not start with extractFolder + File.separator) before creating parent dirs or writing the file. The same `bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh` must then exit non-zero.
parsed_output.summary: Confirmed a Zip Slip / path traversal (CWE-022) in com.alibaba.oneagent.utils.IOUtils.unzip. The method builds the destination via `new File(newPath, entry.getName())` and calls getParentFile().mkdirs() + new FileOutputStream(destFile) without validating that the resolved path stays inside the extraction directory, so a zip entry named `../ESCAPED.txt` is written outside the target folder.

parsed_output.patch_notes: In IOUtils.unzip: captured the extraction directory's canonical path once (destDir.getCanonicalPath()), then for every zip entry compared destFile.getCanonicalPath() against it, requiring it to equal the dir or start with dir + File.separator; otherwise an IOException("Zip slip: <entry>") is thrown before destinationParent.mkdirs() and FileOutputStream. This blocks entries like `../ESCAPED.txt` from writing outside the target. No new imports needed (File and IOException were already imported). Added IOUtilsUnzipTest with a traversal-rejection test and a normal-extraction test to prevent regressions and ensure legitimate archives still extract.
parsed_output.risk_notes: Behavior change is limited to rejecting archive entries that resolve outside the extraction directory; legitimate entries (including nested subdirectories) still extract normally, as verified by the second test. getCanonicalPath() can throw IOException on unusual filesystem states, but unzip already declares throws IOException, so callers are unaffected. Verified: POV now prints SAFE and exits 1 (was VULNERABLE/exit 0), module compiles, and both regression tests pass.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed a Zip Slip / path traversal (CWE-022) in com.alibaba.oneagent.utils.IOUtils.unzip. Each zip entry's resolved destination is now validated against the canonical path of the extraction directory before any parent directories are created or files are written; entries whose canonical path escapes the extraction directory throw an IOException. Added a JUnit regression test covering both the malicious traversal entry and a normal entry.

parsed_output.diff_review: patch_only.diff touches two files. (1) IOUtils.java: introduces `File destDir`, computes `canonicalDestDir = destDir.getCanonicalPath()` once, and for each entry computes `destFile.getCanonicalPath()`, throwing IOException("Zip slip: <entry>") unless it equals destDir or starts with `canonicalDestDir + File.separator`. The check is placed before `destinationParent.mkdirs()` and the FileOutputStream write — the correct pre-write location. Uses the existing `getParentFile().mkdirs()` flow otherwise, so legitimate nested entries still extract. No new imports needed (File/IOException already imported); method already declares `throws IOException`. This is the canonical, minimal Zip Slip remediation. (2) Adds IOUtilsUnzipTest.java with a traversal-rejection test and a normal-extraction test — test-only, appropriate. The pov.diff only adds POV harness files (ZipSlipPov.java, run_pov.sh, compiled classes) and was not modified by the patch. No unrelated behavior, no disabling of functionality, no security risk left.
parsed_output.pov_result: Reran `bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh` via the Docker wrapper. Output: `[POV] unzip threw: java.io.IOException: Zip slip: ../ESCAPED.txt` and `[POV] SAFE: traversal blocked (threw=true, escapedFileExists=false).` with POV_EXIT=1. Matches the orchestrator's pov_after_patch (was VULNERABLE/exit 0 before patch). The malicious `../ESCAPED.txt` entry no longer escapes the extraction directory.

I independently reran the POV (now blocks the traversal, exit 1), the targeted regression test, and the full module suite (7 tests, all passing). The fix is appropriate and does not alter the POV or remove functionality.
